answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the beacon check immediately, the opal audit keeps the resolved set and the meadow replay publishes exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 300 aliases hence pays the reading cost 300 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
